chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, from Aḥmad ibn al-Naḍr, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: concerning
A man who kills his son or his slave—he said: “He is not killed for him, but he is to be beaten severely and banished from the place of his birth.”

key_terms.ابْنَهُ: his son; the filial relation mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.ضَرْبًا شَدِيدًا: a severe beating; the punitive measure imposed
key_terms.عَبْدَهُ: his slave; the owned servant mentioned alongside the son
key_terms.لَا يُقْتَلُ بِهِ: he is not killed for him; i.e., qiṣāṣ is not applied here
key_terms.مَسْقَطِ رَأْسِهِ: the place of his birth; his native locality
key_terms.يَقْتُلُ: kills; the act under legal discussion
key_terms.يُنْفَى: he is banished; removed as a disciplinary punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām on a man who kills his son or his slave?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a man who kills his son or his slave. It states that qiṣāṣ is not carried out against him in this case, but that he is instead subjected to severe beating and banishment from his birthplace.
